messages.author: 849c13fcdba90dbf
messages.subject: variable not recognized, 2 measured variables
parts:
Hi,
I am trying to use the reshape package to change my data format in one
line per subject. There are 4 combination of two factors which will
have to be paired with each of various dependent variables.

I used a small set of test data. First with one measured variable. I
got the error message as below that "variable" was not recognized. I
got a correct result by just listing my two factors (Length &
Complexity) as row variables.

However, I then tried to use 2 measured variables, where I had the
same error in cast, and a different one in recast.
I understand enough the "trim" has to do with the mean function, but I
can't figure out what is wrong.

I am grateful for any help, and apologize for my R ignorance.

Wiltrud

Wiltrud Fassbinder, Ph.D.
Research Associate
Audiology and Speech Pathology
VA Pittsburgh Healthcare System




> ap_test <- read.table("./AP_test2.txt",head = TRUE, sep = "\t")
> melt(ap_test, id=c("subject","Group","Complexity","Length"), measured=c("C1CorNR", "S1CorNR"))
subject Group Complexity Length variable value
1 101 0 1 1 C1CorNR 512
2 101 0 0 2 C1CorNR 656
3 101 0 0 2 C1CorNR 679
4 415 0 0 2 C1CorNR NA
5 415 0 1 2 C1CorNR 1185
6 101 0 1 1 S1CorNR 777
7 101 0 0 2 S1CorNR 1200
8 101 0 0 2 S1CorNR 857
9 415 0 0 2 S1CorNR NA
10 415 0 1 2 S1CorNR 695
> cast(ap_test, subject + Group ~ Length + Complexity + variable, fun.aggregate = mean)
Error: Casting formula contains variables not found in molten data:
variable
>
> ap_test <- read.table("./AP_test2.txt",head = TRUE, sep = "\t")
> recast(ap_test, subject + Group ~ Length + Complexity + variable, fun.aggregate = mean, measure.var = "C1CorNR", "S1CorNR")
Error in mean.default(X[[1L]], ...) :
'trim' must be numeric of length one

>
> ap_test <- read.table("./AP_test2.txt",head = TRUE, sep = "\t")
> recast(ap_test, subject + Group ~ Length + Complexity + variable, fun.aggregate = mean, measure.var = "C1CorNR", "S1CorNR")
Error in mean.default(X[[1L]], ...) :
'trim' must be numeric of length one

> David,
> thank you for your reply, it works, and my analysis life has
> improved considerably. I am sorry to have bothered everyone with
> this trivial issue.

Making the change from a world view that makes everything "global" to
a functional view where you need to explicitly decide what to do with
the output of a function can be "new". Sometimes there is no
assignment and nested functions implicitly process data from the
"inside out". This did not happen to be one of those cases but you
should be aware that will be one of the paradigms as you do more with R.

Best of luck in the New World.

> Wiltrud
